overview: This subsystem is the dev loop and governance layer of ml-vol-estimator, the ML realized volatility forecasting project (registered as productGuid product::982135 in .gs-project.yml). Because most day-to-day work is done by Copilot agents rather than humans, the repo enforces its rules with ordinary code instead of convention. The centerpiece is workspace/lint/lint_all.py, a stdlib-only runner that executes a registry of 21 governance checks in parallel: secexpr safe-mode enforcement, secrets scanning, CoALA memory schema and token budgets, subagent model pins, parity between the ./vol CLI and its documentation, VS Code task hygiene, prompt and schema checks, and more. That same 21-check suite is wired in three places: a local pre-commit hook that always runs, the first step of the GitHub Actions CI job, and the lint-workspace VS Code task. CI itself is explicitly a mirror-only gate: the real remote is GS GitLab where Actions never fire, so ci.yml runs ruff, mypy, and pytest with a 30 percent coverage floor only on the personal GitHub mirror. Agent behavior is governed by .github/copilot-instructions.md: two supported execution surfaces (GS Windows and GS Linux Coder), all file writes confined to workspace/tmp/, all compute routed through the ./vol wrapper or the 45 predefined VS Code tasks that pass arguments via JSON args-files, TDD required for Python changes, and every subagent pinned to a specific Claude model. The workspace/research/ folder is the scientific record that this loop protects: an append-only research journal (capped at 10 entries with an archive) logging trial outcomes such as the trial-067 XGBoost champion at h=1 QLIKE 0.1292, the trial-032 IV tenor-matching win, the trial-055 linear champion ridge_har_cj_iv_0dte at 0.13397, and the GNN program's honest null result, all cross-referenced to trial configs under workspace/configs/.

modules.role: The enforcement point for repo governance: 25 stdlib-only Python scripts, 21 of which are registered in lint_all.py and run in parallel (default 4 workers) with a pass/fail exit code. Checks span security (secexpr safe mode, secrets, doc safety), agent contracts (model pins, args-file contract, wrapper targets, prompts), knowledge hygiene (CoALA memory schema with explicit token budgets, memory priority, index completeness, broken refs), and drift detection (vol CLI vs docs parity, registry drift, VS Code task and markdown compatibility). It is invoked by the pre-commit hook, by CI, and by the lint-workspace VS Code task, so the same gate fires at every stage of the loop.

modules.role: The operational research record for the vol forecasting program. INDEX.md routes every experiment result into trials.yaml (the structured registry, absent from this restore) plus an append-only research-journal.md capped at 10 entries with an overflow archive. The journal records hypotheses, trial outcomes, and retractions with exact QLIKE numbers: the trial-067 XGBoost h=1 champion (0.1292), the trial-032 IV tenor-matching result, the trial-036 retraction after a 5-seed reseed envelope, and the GNN program close-out where five graph trials landed within 1 bp of the har_iv baseline. weekly-progress.md is the manager-facing digest and open-questions.md the research backlog.

modules.role: The task surface for the GS Windows execution surface: tasks.json defines 45 tasks. Roughly 35 wrap GS-internal skills (SECDB inspect/diff/position/translog, SLANG edit/review/eval/copilot, GitLab MR/search/pipelines, Symphony, Prime, NDS infra, data-ingest, feature-build, model-train, evaluate, backtest) each launching a skill's task script with parameters passed through a JSON args-file in workspace/tmp/, so agents never compose free-form shell. Three vol-* tasks run the ./vol wrapper (test, lint, typecheck) cross-platform via vol.cmd on Windows, and a post-open task auto-runs on folderOpen.

glossary.definition: Quasi-likelihood loss, the project's headline volatility forecast metric; it heavily penalizes under-predicting variance and is robust to noise in the realized variance proxy. The tournament reports Patton QLIKE alongside panel Diebold-Mariano tests and a 5 percent model confidence set.
Heterogeneous Autoregressive model: a linear regression of future realized volatility on daily, weekly, and monthly RV averages (log_rv_d/w/m), the standard baseline every model here must beat.
The 4-parameter HAR extended with ATM implied volatility; a long-running champion baseline that outperformed the 128-feature LightGBM at all horizons in the IV sanity check.
Diebold-Mariano test of equal predictive accuracy between two forecast series; trial results quote DM p-values to show whether a QLIKE gap is statistically significant.

The structured agent memory scheme (from the Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents framing): distilled knowledge files with validated frontmatter, domain folders, and hard token budgets enforced by validate_memory.py.
A GS-internal data access command invoked by skills; the lint suite forces its safe mode by default and allows the --full flag only in explicitly whitelisted files.

A sanctioned environment where agents may run: S-A is the GS Windows desktop with VS Code tasks, S-B is the GS Linux Coder workspace with the ./vol wrapper, and S-C (GitHub cloud agent) is unsupported.

The convention that VS Code tasks pass all parameters through a JSON file under workspace/tmp/ instead of shell arguments, making skill invocations reproducible and lintable (enforced by lint_args_contract.py).
